```{r}
#| label: setup
source("info_valuebox.R")
config <- read_value_box_config()
statements <- readr::read_csv("input/example_statements.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## At a glance

These examples use the supplied statements to demonstrate the designs.
Confirm the figures, reporting periods and sources before publication.

```{r}
#| label: four-value-boxes
# Pass display text explicitly; the functions do not interpret the statistics.
boxes <- list(
  info_value_box(
    title = "Risky drinking", value = "2.0\u00d7", value_note = "the proportion",
    type = "comparative", demographic_var = "sex",
    context = "Males vs females",
    description = statements$example_statement[[1]], config = config
  ),
  info_value_box(
    title = "Hospitalisation rates", value = "25.5%", value_note = "higher",
    type = "comparative", demographic_var = "aria",
    context = "Remote areas vs major cities",
    description = statements$example_statement[[2]], config = config
  ),
  info_value_box(
    title = "Risky drinking", value = "5.3%", direction = "decrease",
    type = "trend", demographic_var = "persons",
    context = "In adults, 2012 to 2022",
    description = statements$example_statement[[4]], config = config
  ),
  info_value_box(
    title = "Smoking prevalence", value = "10.5%",
    type = "domain_statistic", demographic_var = "smoking",
    context = "In Queensland high school students",
    description = statements$example_statement[[7]], config = config
  )
)
info_value_box_layout(boxes) # Four cards automatically become two rows of two.
```

## Three key facts

```{r}
#| label: three-value-boxes
three_boxes <- list(
  info_value_box(
    title = "Potentially preventable hospitalisations", value = "6.4%",
    type = "domain_statistic", demographic_var = "hospitalisation",
    context = "Of all hospitalisations",
    description = statements$example_statement[[8]], config = config
  ),
  info_value_box(
    title = "Smoking rates", value = "53.4%", direction = "decrease",
    type = "trend", demographic_var = "male",
    context = "In adult males",
    description = statements$example_statement[[9]], config = config
  ),
  info_value_box(
    title = "Hospitalisations", value = "51.5%", direction = "increase",
    type = "trend", demographic_var = "persons",
    context = "Adult hospitalisation rates",
    description = statements$example_statement[[5]], config = config
  )
)
info_value_box_layout(three_boxes) # One row of three on a wide page.
```

## Two key facts

```{r}
#| label: two-value-boxes
info_value_box_layout(boxes[[1]], boxes[[2]]) # One row of two.
```

## Creating boxes from a table

For pages maintained as data, use one row per box and column names matching
the function arguments. The same config is shared across all boxes.

```{r}
#| label: table-driven-value-boxes
#| echo: true
facts <- tibble::tibble(
  title = c("Hospitalisation rates", "Chronic disease hospitalisations"),
  value = c("18.9%", "18.0%"),
  type = c("comparative", "trend"),
  demographic_var = c("seifa", "persons"),
  context = c("Most disadvantaged vs most advantaged areas", "Seven chronic diseases"),
  description = statements$example_statement[c(3, 6)],
  value_note = list("higher", NULL),
  direction = list(NULL, "decrease")
)
facts |>
  purrr::pmap(info_value_box, config = config) |>
  info_value_box_layout()
```
